us: White House won't confirm reported refiners meeting · Embassy Beirut demands Hezbollah disarm · CENTCOM sustains Osprey ops
effects: 3rd tanker struck this week · UKMTO risk 'SEVERE' for the strait · 6,000 sailors stranded · Trade −35%, inflation 66%
iran: Gharibabadi: deal reached, gated on Islamabad MoU · Khamenei flags 'economic and livelihood challenges' · Pezeshkian: revive June 17 MoU · 'prepared for any scenario'
tldr: Iran declared its Hormuz understanding with Oman 'reached' — but said it will not take effect until the US implements the Islamabad MoU, keeping the strait 'closed' with any transit 'in coordination with Iran' — as a third tanker in a week was struck by an unknown projectile 12nm north of al-Khasab. Mojtaba Khamenei, unseen publicly since February, acknowledged the 'economic and livelihood challenges' for the first time, with Pezeshkian putting foreign trade down ~35% and inflation at 66% while urging revival of the lapsed June 17 MoU. Banque Misr said it is reviewing the FinCEN proposal 'with utmost seriousness' while its UAE branches keep serving customers. No confirmed strikes inside Iran — the 30th consecutive day — and no new US designations or CENTCOM accounting.

events.title: Third tanker in a week struck by unknown projectile 12nm north of al-Khasab
events.summary: A tanker was struck by an unknown projectile off Oman on Saturday — 12nm north of al-Khasab — with no injuries or environmental damage reported, per UKMTO, which issued its warning late on Sunday (delayed reporting). No attribution; authorities investigating; no Iranian claim or denial found. It is the week's third commercial-vessel strike (Monday's Ash Shishah, Wednesday's Kuwaiti-connected vessel). UKMTO's accompanying report keeps the strait at SEVERE risk, says traffic remains 'significantly reduced' with operators increasingly favouring the Northern route, and logs continuing IRGC harassment — drone overflights, targeted surveillance of merchant vessels, occasional radio transmissions. Single wire report (dpa) carrying UKMTO's X post — treat attribution as unknown.

events.title: Gharibabadi: Oman Hormuz understanding 'reached' — but not until US honors Islamabad MoU
events.summary: Iran's deputy foreign minister said Saturday that Iran and Oman have reached an understanding over the Strait of Hormuz, but it 'will not be implemented until the United States fulfills its commitments under the Islamabad MoU' — the June agreement Qatar and Pakistan helped broker, which Pezeshkian separately urged reviving on state TV. 'The Strait of Hormuz remains closed, and any vessel passing through the strait does so in coordination with Iran'; Tehran will continue what it calls 'defensive measures' and is 'prepared for any scenario.' Gharibabadi framed the weekend's Qatari and Pakistani visits as aimed at determining whether the parties can return to implementing the MoU's commitments. First 'reached' claim for the corridor, now gated on Washington; CENTCOM maintains Iran does not control the strait. Per Iran International citing Iranian media, carried by Fox — no independent confirmation of the 'reached' claim.

events.title: Khamenei flags 'economic and livelihood challenges'; Pezeshkian: trade down ~35%
events.summary: In a written statement attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei — not seen publicly since the Feb 28 attack that killed his father — the supreme leader said 'there is the need to seriously address the chain of economic and livelihood challenges, such as inflation, unemployment, management of prices and the market for goods and services,' as the Outcast campaign mounts. Pezeshkian told state media exports and imports slumped nearly 35% under sanctions and the naval blockade, then called on state TV for revival of the June 17 interim MoU: 'We can solve our problems and gain our privileges with the memorandum of understanding' — the short-lived deal under which Iran sold ~90M barrels. Annual inflation hit 66% last month. Tehran signalled no retreat, calling diplomacy and defence 'two complementary, coordinated and inseparable wings.'

events.title: Banque Misr pushes back: review 'with utmost seriousness', UAE branches keep serving customers
events.summary: The Egyptian state bank's UAE branch — FinCEN's proposed cut from US correspondent banking over ~$1.8B processed for 103 companies allegedly tied to Iranian shadow-banking networks — said Saturday it is reviewing the notice 'with utmost seriousness and attention' while continuing to serve customers. Egypt's central bank said it and the foreign ministry are in contact with US officials, noting the measure is limited to Banque Misr UAE's US dollar transactions with correspondent banks. First public response to the campaign's first bank-facing move; Cairo and the host supervisor so far answer the 'auction' in public, with no final rule in place.

events.title: Khamenei Unity Week letter: Gulf rulers should 'identify your real enemy'
events.summary: In a Telegram statement marking Islamic Unity Week, Mojtaba Khamenei urged Muslim nations — especially Gulf rulers — to unite against their 'real enemy,' advocating mutual defence and joint cooperation, and asking whether 'rogues without identity' would have dared covet Gulf lands had the region been 'united under the flag of Islam.' It echoes his Friday ban on 'discouraging statements' that weaken public and national morale. Timing note: Economic Times syndication ran Saturday Aug 29; the Independent's Reuters bulletin published Aug 30 — treat the letter's landing as approximate to the weekend.

events.title: Tehran signals dialogue path open; acting defense minister teases 'surprises'
events.summary: Ambassador to Germany Majid Nili said Tehran is ready to pursue dialogue with the US — 'the path of dialogue and engagement based on mutual respect is still being pursued' (IRNA via Middle East Eye) — following Araghchi's Friday X post that 'putting diplomacy back on track isn't impossible' if Washington builds trust and upholds commitments. Acting defense minister Brig. Gen. Majid Ebn al-Reza (Tasnim): adversaries 'will become aware of Iran's surprises in due time.' Pezeshkian, marking six months of war (IRIB): Iran does not welcome war, 'but we will stand strong against any aggressor, and no power can force a nation that stands with all its might and will to surrender.'

events.title: IMO: 6,000 sailors stranded, 19 seafarers killed, 70+ attacks on shipping at six months
events.summary: The UN's maritime agency said Friday that at least 6,000 sailors remain stranded aboard hundreds of ships in the Persian Gulf six months into the war, that 19 seafarers have been killed since Feb 28, and that at least 70 attacks on international shipping have been recorded — carried on Fox's Aug 29 page. The war's cumulative toll on commercial shipping, quantified by the agency; no follow-up US or Iranian comment found.

events.title: Trump reportedly to convene refiners and fuel retailers Sept 1 on gas prices; White House won't confirm
events.summary: Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that Trump will meet US oil refiners and fuel retailers next week on efforts to lower consumer prices; Bloomberg separately put the meeting on the afternoon of Tuesday Sept 1 with representatives of at least 10 fuel makers and distributors. Asked about it, a White House official did not confirm: 'The Trump Administration will make a decision that is best for consumers, farmers, and energy supply chains.' The reported session tracks the war's pump-price pressure (AAA ~$4.09/gal Friday, per the Aug 28 report).
